item.title: Real Madrid legend’s son continues to take major strides towards first-team breakthrough at club
item.description: Real Madrid legend’s son continues to take major strides towards first-team breakthrough at club Real Madrid youngster Enzo Alves is rapidly building a reputation of his own, with AS reporting that the son of club legend Marcelo is attracting attention across Europe after an impressive rise through the academy. The outlet mentions that the 17-year-old striker has scored more than 150 goals in a Real Madrid shirt and continues to strengthen his case as one of the club’s most promising young attacking talents. His latest statement came against RB Leipzig in the UEFA Youth League on October 21, when he opened the scoring in Real Madrid’s 5-2 victory. His composed finish in the 15th minute helped the reigning champions secure a third consecutive win in the competition. Enzo Alves beginning to step out of Marcelo’s shadow Comparisons with a famous parent are inevitable in sport, but Enzo is increasingly giving everyone reasons to assess him on his own merits. While Marcelo made his name as an attack-minded left-back, his son is developing as a forward, using his movement and instincts in the penalty area to influence matches. His progress at Valdebebas has gathered momentum throughout 2026. After making his UEFA Youth League debut in November 2025, Enzo has continued to climb the academy ladder, earning opportunities at higher levels and attracting growing attention for his goalscoring. Real Madrid’s trust in his potential was explained in January, when he signed his first professional contract with the club. The agreement followed a period of progress that had already seen him train and play across different youth levels, with the club keen to retain a talent it considers valuable for the future. Real Madrid have high hopes for their academy striker Enzo Alves is gaining attention at Real Madrid. (Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images) It is to be remembered that Alvaro Arbeloa previously gave him a chance with Castilla before moving into the senior coaching structure, providing the youngster with experience at a higher competitive level. His route to the first team, however, remains a long-term ambition rather than an immediate guarantee. The next major test could come internationally. The FIFA Under-17 World Cup is scheduled to take place in Qatar from November 19 to December 13, 2026, and Enzo is tipped for involvement with Spain’s youth setup. Indeed, Enzo still has significant work ahead, but his goals, recent Youth League performance and new professional contract show that his progress is being taken seriously.

item.title: Packers’ Matt LaFleur gushes about Jahmyr Gibbs’ ‘elite’ skillset before Lions clash
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Packers’ Matt LaFleur gushes about Jahmyr Gibbs’ ‘elite’ skillset before Lions clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers are looking confident heading into Week 7 . Green Bay is 4-2 on the season and riding a three-game winning streak after struggling to start the year. However, the Packers will not be overconfident when facing an NFC North rival on Sunday . Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is not going to underestimate Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs in Week 7. He gushed about Gibbs’ elite abilities ahead of this weekend’s matchup. “You cannot relax for one second with this guy. … He has elite change of direction skills,” LaFleur said about Gibbs on Thursday, per ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LaFleur added that Gibbs could probably play slot receiver if Detroit asked him to. The Packers would be wise to focus on shutting down Gibbs, who is by far the most explosive player on Detroit’s offense. Gibbs has 105 carries for 504 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through five games this year. That is on top of 27 receptions for 243 receiving yards and two touchdowns through the air. The Lions run a large chunk of their offense through the speedy running back. Once Gibbs establishes himself in a game, Detroit’s entire offense opens up. If the Packers do not put a lid on Gibbs’ production, they could be in for a real shootout. Fortunately, the Packers looked equipped to go toe to toe with the Lions. Green Bay’s defense has been playing well recently, even with Micah Parsons still on the sideline. They should also get Josh Jacobs back this week , which could improve Green Bay’s terrible rushing attack. If the Packers can control the clock with their running game, they can suck the air out of the ball. As a result, they can slow down Gibbs by simply keeping him off the field entirely. It will be exciting to see who comes out on top of this huge NFC North showdown on Sunday. Packers at Lions kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET on Oct. 25 from Ford Field in Detroit. Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme. FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino (PA) Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino . “The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.” Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement. “We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice. “Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision. “The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.” Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪 The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance. "Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. "This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement. "This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. item.title: ‘Classy’ – Skip Bayless gives his take on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s 20-point streak ending
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s 20-point scoring streak came to an end on Thursday when the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Denver Nuggets. The Thunder are now 2-0 after picking up a 96-84 victory but the main talking point coming out of the game has not been the result. Instead, it has centred on Gilgeous-Alexander failing to score 20 points or more in a regular season game for the first time in nearly two years. He scored 17 on the night before subbing himself out of the game, which Skip Bayless has now reacted to and called a ‘classy move’. Speaking in a video shared on X/Twitter, he said: “What a great, classy move by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. For 126 straight games, he had scored at least 20 points. “It’s the most unbelievable record in sports. I believe it will never, ever be broken. It was 15 more games than Wilt Chamberlain had in 63/64. I so appreciated the way it ended because Shai, with a minute and 43 seconds left, had 17 points and had heated up in the fourth quarter with 11 points and I’m thinking, ‘He’s going to do it again’. “The Thunder were up 17 and the Nuggets took all their starters out and just gave up and Shai just marched straight to the bench and say ‘no, that’s enough, I struggled all night’. He was pretty terrible for most of the night by his standards, didn’t score a bucket in the first half, 0-7. “Denver always does a good to great job on him, and they did a great job tonight. They really make him work. I think he demonstrated, ‘I could still get this if I wanted it,’ and this is just me, I think he wanted Denver to break the record. He appreciates and respects how they play him defensively.” The Thunder will now return to the court on Sunday against the LA Clippers, who are 1-0 ahead of their next game versus the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday. item.title: Porro back for Spurs but De Zerbi raises doubts over duo’s involvement against Chelsea
item.description: Porro back for Spurs but De Zerbi raises doubts over duo’s involvement against Chelsea Pedro Porro is back available for Tottenham, but Roberto De Zerbi has raised doubts over the fitness of James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski for the clash with Chelsea. Porro has not played since before the last international break but is in line to feature against Spurs’ rivals. “Pedro is back, Robertson is available, Marmoush is good, Solanke is good,” De Zerbi said. However, De Zerbi confirmed that Lucas Bergvall, Savio and Destiny Udogie remain sidelined this weekend. Maddison, meanwhile, missed the first three days of training this week and De Zerbi is unsure whether he will be ready. “In the first three days Maddison didn’t work with us, so I don’t know if he’s ready for tomorrow,” he said. “We can play with Mathys Tel or Marmoush inside or Gallagher, we have more solutions considering Pedro Porro can play.” Kulusevski is also not yet fully clear, having too not fully trained after returning to action from around a year-and-a-half out on Monday night against Coventry . “Kulusevski worked well but in the first day he stayed individually,” De Zerbi said. The Spurs boss stressed he does not want to take unnecessary risks with players given the number of injuries across football. “Like I said many times, I don’t want to take risks because if you analyse this period of football, you can see many injuries,” he said. “Not for Tottenham, for everyone. item.title: Ian Poulter quits LIV Golf as exodus continues
item.description: Ian Poulter has become the latest high-profile player to exit the floundering LIV Golf circuit. The breakaway league is hoping to avoid Chapter 11 bankruptcy by trying to establish ‘LIV 2.0’ with new investment, following the decision by Saudi Arabia ’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) to cut its funding for the circuit this April. LIV is to make a decision on whether to cease operations or proceed with a scaled-down model this month, with the 25 October deadline for players to confirm their interest in staying on rapidly approaching. Poulter, who co-captained the Majesticks team, has announced he will not be part of the league’s new incarnation. He recently appeared at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, his first start at a DP World Tour event in more than three years, while an exit from LIV appeared more likely after he settled fines with the DP World Tour reportedly worth over $1m. The two-time World Golf Championship winner said in a statement: “I wanted everyone to hear it direct from me that I have decided to not move forward with being part of LIV 2.0. Needless to say, it was a tough decision and one I thought about and discussed at length with my family and team. “Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career.” The Englishman conceded that LIV Golf had “divided opinion” but said what he achieved while on the tour “is something I will forever be proud of”, thanking the fans, his teammates and staff for their support. He continued: “I’m looking forward to spending more time with my family, continuing to develop The Postman YouTube channel, sharing more of my life, golf, experiences and competing in some senior events.” The 50-year-old also said he was looking forward to spending more time golfing with sons Luke and Joshua, with the former pursuing a career as a professional. “Having spent so many years travelling the world chasing my own golfing dreams, the opportunity to now spend more time supporting my boys as they chase theirs is something that means a great deal to me,” he said.

item.title: Report: Milan want to bring Athekame back from Lyon loan but face reluctance
item.description: Report: Milan want to bring Athekame back from Lyon loan but face reluctance Reports in Italy claim that Milan have explored the possibility of bringing Zachary Athekame back from his loan spell with Olympique Lyonnais ahead of schedule, but both the French club and the player are not keen on the suggestion according to the latest updates. Report: Milan want Athekame back from Lyon, but club and player say no Athekame joined Lyon on loan for the 2026-27 season back in August, having joined the Rossoneri in a €10m deal from Young Boys the previous summer. His loan to Lyon does not include an option to buy. PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Zachary Athekame of AC Milan in action during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) He has since gone on to provide two goals and three assists from right-back in his first seven matches in Ligue 1 and according to reports from La Gazzetta dello Sport and Calciomercato.com , the Rossoneri are keen to bring the Switzerland international back from his loan deal in January. This is largely due to concerns regarding Samuel Chukwueze’s latest injury . The Nigerian has started six out of seven Serie A matches at right wing-back under Ruben Amorim so far in 2026-27, but is now facing two to three months on the sidelines with a hamstring injury. According to Calciomercato, Milan representatives have recently been in direct contact with their counterparts in Lyon to discuss the possibility of bringing Athekame back from his loan spell in January. DECINES-CHARPIEU, FRANCE – OCTOBER 15: Zachary Athekame of Olympique Lyonnais reacts to a play during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Olympique Lyonnais and Crystal Palace FC at OL Stadium on October 15, 2026 in Decines-Charpieu, France. (Photo by Pauline Figuet/Getty Images) However, both the player and his loan club do not seem convinced by this idea: Athekame has become a key player under Paulo Fonseca and the former Milan coach does not want to lose his first-choice right-back, who has been described as one of the best in France so far this season. Athekame himself is reportedly keen to continue with Lyon, where he has enjoyed an excellent start, and is only interested in returning to Milan once the 2026-27 season is over.

Conte shuts down talk of imminent return The managerial merry-go-round has been spinning rapidly in recent weeks, with Conte at the very centre of the conversation. Following his successful tenure at Napoli, the Italian tactician has been widely touted as the primary candidate to take over at Man Utd , where Michael Carrick is under immense pressure, or return to Juventus should the club part ways with Luciano Spalletti. However, Conte has now moved to dismiss claims that a deal with any new employer is close to being finalised. In a detailed statement shared across his social media platforms, the former Chelsea and Inter manager made it clear that he is in no rush to step back into the dugout. Gibson’s departure came just hours after the Red Wings recalled Michal Postava from the Grand Rapids Griffins under emergency conditions because backup goaltender Daniil Tarasov was already dealing with an injury. That meant Postava, who had never appeared in an NHL game, suddenly found himself protecting Detroit’s lead in Vancouver. Oct 10, 2026; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Detroit Red Wings goalie John Gibson (36) looks on during warm-up before the game against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell Centre. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) John Gibson Exits Red Wings Victory With Injury Gibson started Thursday’s game and stopped four of the five shots he faced through the first two periods. Detroit dominated much of the action, including a remarkable second period in which the Canucks failed to register a single shot on goal. However, Gibson did not return to the crease for the final 20 minutes. The Red Wings initially described the issue as an upper-body injury, but head coach Todd McLellan provided additional information afterward. According to the team’s official postgame update , McLellan explained that Gibson was dealing with an issue involving his eye. “He had something in his eye. They’re still looking at it,” McLellan said. The coach also indicated that he learned about the situation late in the second intermission, leaving Detroit little time to prepare for a goaltending change. The extent of Gibson’s injury and his availability for Saturday’s game against Calgary have not yet been determined. Michal Postava Makes Unexpected NHL Debut The timing of Gibson’s departure was particularly unusual because Detroit had already experienced another goaltending injury earlier in the week. As we previously reported following Thursday’s emergency roster moves , the Red Wings recalled Postava from Grand Rapids after Tarasov developed an undisclosed injury. McLellan later explained that Tarasov had aggravated something during Wednesday’s practice, prompting the organization to bring in additional insurance. That decision became extremely important just one day later. Postava entered Thursday’s game at the beginning of the third period and stopped seven of eight shots, helping Detroit preserve its three-goal victory. The 24-year-old had entered the week with an impressive 4-0-0 record, a 1.25 goals-against average, and a .954 save percentage in Grand Rapids. McLellan praised the rookie for responding to a situation neither he nor the coaching staff anticipated. “That’s not the way we planned it,” McLellan acknowledged after the victory. The game’s official scoring recap confirmed that Postava made seven saves in his NHL debut while Lucas Raymond led Detroit offensively with two goals and an assist. Red Wings Face Uncertainty Ahead of Calgary Game The encouraging news is that Tarasov’s injury may not be as serious as initially feared. McLellan described his backup goaltender as day-to-day following Thursday’s game, indicating that Detroit would continue evaluating his condition before making another roster decision. As we previously examined during Detroit’s early-season goaltending debate , Tarasov has been one of the team’s most impressive performers between the pipes. Losing both Gibson and Tarasov for any extended period would place significant pressure on Detroit’s organizational depth, although there has been no indication that either player faces a lengthy absence. For now, Postava provides an intriguing alternative if additional help is needed. The Red Wings improved to 4-3-3 with Thursday’s victory and have collected points in six consecutive games. Their next challenge comes Saturday night against the Calgary Flames, followed by a Monday matchup with the Edmonton Oilers. Detroit’s recent momentum is encouraging, but its goaltending situation has suddenly become one of the biggest questions surrounding the team. What began as a precautionary emergency recall Thursday morning turned into an unexpected NHL debut that evening. Now the Red Wings must determine whether their regular goaltenders will be healthy enough to finish the road trip.

item.title: Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. reportedly charged with marijuana possession
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MO - Anthony Richardson Sr.of the Indianapolis Colts before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Anthony Richardson Sr. of the Indianapolis Colts is facing a misdemeanor charge for possession of marijuana following an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Indiana, according to FOX59 . “We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information,” the Colts said in a statement. “We will have no further comment at this time.” Court documents obtained by FOX59/CBS4 show that charges were filed on Monday, a week after police officers stopped Richardson's black 2023 Dodge Charger. The vehicle's registration was reportedly expired and was assigned to a different car. According to police, the car pulled over to the side of the road and officers noticed the "odor of marijuana" as they approached. Richardson reportedly admitted that he did smoke marijuana in the car so as to not do so in front of his children. He also told police that he possessed a small amount of marijuana in the car. The quarterback was handcuffed after exiting the car and officers proceeded with searching the vehicle. A small mason jar was reportedly found containing a substance believed to be marijuana and a bag of THC-infused gummies that was opened. The substance reportedly tested positive for THC. Richardson was also cited for the expired registration. A hearing was scheduled for Dec. 9, but has since been waived. A bench trial will be held on Jan. 2027. Richardson is the second Colts player to have a run-in with police this season. Wide receiver Keenan Allen was charged with two misdemeanors following his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.

Having that honesty with everybody, it just makes everybody want to play better for each other.” Last season, when Bowen was fired in November, it became obvious that his less-than-direct approach was the wrong one for these Giants. For now, Pinnock — a sixth-year safety — said the Giants’ players left his meeting with resolve. “That was probably the best tough meeting to have,” he told NJ.com. “I’ve been in those type of situations where it’s just straight finger pointing [from the coach]. And you walk out, and everybody has their side remarks, like: ‘Ah, man, whatever.’ Nah, that was positive, and it was needed. It’s not like somebody feels targeted.” Pinnock said this stems from the tight relationships Wilson, 44, has built with his players. “It’s going to feel personal if I don’t know you,” Pinnock said. “Dennard, he talks to all of us on and off the field, jokes with us, learns our humor. He knows his personnel, so he knows how to get the best out of everybody. I think it was a good meeting.” So how does Pinnock think the Giants’ defense will respond in Houston? “How we should: Go get a W,” he said. item.title: Kovac praises Schlotterbeck's commitment
item.description: Kovac praises Schlotterbeck's commitment All the players who made the trip came through the match in Baku unscathed. “Yesterday was a day off from training. That was very important after all the kilometres we had to cover,” says BVB coach Niko Kovac. Konstantinos Karetsas had already missed out in midweek due to a ligament injury in his foot and will also be unavailable against Eintracht. Kovac could not yet say whether he would be an option for Tuesday’s cup match against Bremen. Kaua Prates has a minor muscle problem. Justin Lerma remains sidelined with a more serious muscle injury. Nico Schlotterbeck returned early from international duty with an ankle injury but was back on the pitch straight after the international break. He only sat out the match against Bodø/Glimt to manage his workload. Speaking about the centre-back, Kovac says: “He has pain in his ankle from time to time. It can’t possibly have healed 100 per cent yet. But you can see how important he is to the team and how he gives everything for them. item.title: Gasperini’s Faith in Emanuele Lulli Pays Off as Roma Pursue New Deal
item.description: ROME, ITALY - OCTOBER 17: Emanuele Lulli of Roma celebrates his goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on October 17, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Image Photo Agency/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we all hope Roma’s return to the Champions League will usher in a new era of free-wheeling spending on the transfer market, sustained success still requires significant building from within. Homegrown players are not only more cost-effective, but they also bring what we might call corporate knowledge: insight and investment in the club’s values. These combined factors foster a sense of identity and camaraderie, while freeing up funds to acquire the finishing pieces the club needs to achieve its long-range goals. We’ve seen this approach work over the years with players as varied as Francesco Totti and Alessandro Florenzi, while talents like Niccolò Pisilli will ensure that Roma’s identity remains intact. And thanks to his breakout campaign, we can now add Emmanuele Lulli to that list. The 19-year-old wing-back just missed the cut in this summer’s U-23 countdown, but Lulli has been a hot name on prospect radars for the past couple of seasons. All Lulli needed was a manager willing to give him a chance to learn and grow on the job, one willing to ride the highs and lows that come with relying on teenage talents. Enter Gian Piero Gasperini. Never one to shy away from relying on unproven players, Gasperini has thrown Lulli into the deep end this season, and Roma is reaping the rewards. With five appearances, including four starts in Roma’s first seven league matches, Lulli is flourishing under Gasperini’s tutelage, flashing an impressive blend of attacking prowess and defensive acumen. Lulli reached his early-season peak last weekend, scoring his first professional goal in the Giallorossi’s 2-0 win at the Olimpico against Genoa. The 19-year-old Roman’s future is looking brighter by the day, so much so that the club is already making moves to ensure he remains in their warm embrace. item.title: Vikings’ Jauan Jennings Has New Potential Trade Landing Spot
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Getty The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Getty The Minnesota Vikings could send Jauan Jennings to the Washington Commanders to give quarterback Jayden Daniels another pass target. Getty There has been no shortage of suggested trade destinations for Minnesota Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings. Another one, though, has seemingly emerged this week. Heavy Sports proposes the Vikings trade Jennings to the Washington Commanders in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick. The Vikings signed Jennings to a 1-year, $8 million deal over the offseason. Pundits expected the veteran to supply much-needed depth for Minnesota as a WR3. But Jennings has received just five targets in four games this season. He has caught two of those targets for nine yards. Why Vikings Could Part With WR Jauan Jennings at NFL Trade Deadline Getty The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Jennings just simply isn’t working out for the Vikings this season. He’s barely involved in the offense. Over the past two weeks, Myles Price has started receiving more targets than the veteran. That makes Jennings a trade candidate even though the Vikings are contending. Enough teams have a need at receiver that Jennings could be in demand. With a Jennings trade, Minnesota could basically buy a draft pick. Meaning, the financial investment the team made in Jennings for the first half of this season will give the team an extra Day 3 selection. If the Vikings deal Jennings, the team could move forward with Price and Tai Felton as their options behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison . What Jennings Could Bring to Commanders Getty The Minnesota Vikings could send Jauan Jennings to the Washington Commanders to give quarterback Jayden Daniels another pass target. Jennings is a potential trade target for the Commanders because the team just lost veteran starting receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon on Monday night. Teams don’t typically make trades within the same conference. But the Vikings might not have an issue with that since it doesn’t appear likely they will compete with the Commanders for a playoff spot. Washington is 1-4-1 entering this week while Minnesota sits at 5-0. The Commanders could see Jennings as a short-term McLaurin replacement. Jennings could finish the season with Washington and potentially be a lot more productive than he has been in Minnesota. Last season, Jennings posted 55 catches, 643 receiving yards and a career-best nine touchdowns. Jennings reached new heights with 77 catches and 975 receiving yards during 2024. item.title: Raiders news: Andrew Janocko sees Michael Mayer as valuable piece
item.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing for their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams. It will be their chance to end a three-game losing streak after starting 3-0. Michael Mayer will look to duplicate his Week 6 performance. He had a career game last week for the Silver and Black. 95 receiving yards was his highest total since being drafted into the NFL. He has become a vital piece in the passing game. The Raiders coaching staff is not surprised. Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko spoke of his value to the team during his press conference on Thursday. “Yeah, Mike [Mayer] is a valuable piece to this team because of the person that Mike is, starting with that. So, you start with an ultimate competitor. You start with somebody that comes to work each and every single day, and then you take the football skill set and how he has developed as a player, how he’s developing in a leadership role. He’s going to be a part of our success going forward.” His stats this season were expected. Janocko loves his work and study habits as Mayer is in the front row during team meetings. “I think you just watch Mike [Mayer work every single day in everything he does, run game, pass game protections, and how he takes nothing lightly. Watching Mike, Mike sits in the front row of the meeting rooms and just watching him take note and how he pays attention, and then it applies on the field. It’s just that’s what you look for in a consummate pro.“ Raider Nation should expect Mayer to keep producing in this offense. If teams try to take away Bowers, Mayer’s production will keep rising. item.title: Today in Motorsport History, October 23: MotoGP Lost Marco Simoncelli at Sepang in 2011
item.description: A pack of riders leans through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Harvey Tan Villarino / Pexels Marco Simoncelli died at Sepang 15 years ago today, on October 23, 2011, after a crash on the second lap of the Malaysian Grand Prix. He was 24. The race was red-flagged, a restart was pencilled in and then dropped, and one lap was all MotoGP got. No winner was declared and no points were awarded. It was the first death in the premier class since Daijiro Kato’s at the 2003 Japanese Grand Prix, and it came just over a year after Moto2 rider Shoya Tomizawa died at Misano. The season he was finally having Simoncelli arrived in 2011 as the 2008 250cc world champion, in his second year with the San Carlo Honda Gresini team after finishing eighth in the 2010 standings. This was the year it came together. He took pole at Catalunya in June, stood on the podium at Brno, and a week before Sepang finished second to Casey Stoner at Phillip Island, his best result in the class. He was sixth in the championship, he had signed to stay with Gresini for 2012 on a Honda RC213V, and he was the satellite rider who could actually run with the factory bikes. Phillip Island, for what it is worth, would produce a very different kind of Sunday two years later, which we covered in our Márquez black-flag story . It had also been a heavy week for the sport. Dan Wheldon was killed in the IndyCar finale at Las Vegas on October 16, the same day Stoner clinched his second MotoGP title in Australia. Paddocks do not recover from a week like that, and Sepang was the next stop. Sunday at Sepang Fact Detail Date Sunday, October 23, 2011 Event Malaysian Grand Prix, round 17 of the 2011 MotoGP season Circuit Sepang International Circuit, Malaysia (5.543 km) MotoGP pole Dani Pedrosa, Repsol Honda (2:01.462) Crash Lap 2, exit of Turn 11 Riders involved Marco Simoncelli, Colin Edwards, Valentino Rossi Declared dead 4:56pm local time Race result Abandoned after one lap; no winner, no points awarded 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Sepang International Circuit statement, October 25, 2011; MotoGP race records. Pedrosa took pole with a Repsol Honda lockout of the front row, and Stoner took the lead from Pedrosa and Andrea Dovizioso at the start. On lap two, Simoncelli, running fourth, lost the front end on the exit of the Turn 11 right-hander. Bike and rider slid across the track and into the path of Colin Edwards (Tech 3 Yamaha) and Valentino Rossi (Ducati), who had no room to avoid him. Both hit him. Edwards suffered a separated shoulder, and Rossi got his bike back to the pits. Simoncelli’s helmet came off in the impact. Two riders trade lines through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Cipriano Fernandes / Pexels The race was red-flagged immediately. MotoGP medical director Michele Macchiagodena said Simoncelli went into cardiac arrest in the ambulance, and doctors worked on him for about 45 min

MotoGP medical director Michele Macchiagodena said Simoncelli went into cardiac arrest in the ambulance, and doctors worked on him for about 45 minutes before declaring him dead at 4:56pm local time. A 4:30pm restart had been planned, then delayed, then cancelled. Sepang’s chairman said two days later that the circuit and Dorna had agreed the race could not continue, and that the circuit had followed every precaution required by the FIM, the Malaysian motorsport authority and Dorna. Stoner, who had taken the lead at the start, said watching the footage left him feeling “sick inside.” Why it mattered Two deaths in just over a year, in two different classes, changed the tone of the paddock. Simoncelli was one of the most popular riders in it, and “Super Sic” was the name on his team’s own tribute that night. The crash itself began as an ordinary front-end slide at a corner exit, the kind of fall riders walk away from most weekends. That is what made it so hard for the sport to absorb. It also sharpened a question that never fully went away: how much protection a helmet can promise when everything goes wrong at once. Simoncelli’s helmet separated from his head in the impact, and the helmet’s developer later attributed that to the chin strap tearing out. That discussion has not stopped. For a current example of how differently racing’s rulebooks treat helmet life, see our look at the helmet that expires differently in every rulebook . A rider leans a bike through a corner. Illustrative image, not from Sepang. Photo: Harvey Tan Villarino / Pexels What changed, and what didn’t Be careful with the word “changed.” In the sources I could verify, the crash is not tied to a single rule rewrite. Sepang’s own statement said the circuit would work with the FIM and Dorna on whether further rider-safety measures were possible, and that is as specific as the official record gets. What did change is easier to see and name: Misano’s circuit was renamed Misano World Circuit Marco Simoncelli, announced in November 2011 and made official the following year. The Fondazione Marco Simoncelli 58 was set up in his name, and his father Paolo later started the Sic58 Squadra Corse team. On September 8, 2016, ahead of the San Marino Grand Prix at Misano, Dorna CEO Carmelo Ezpeleta and Paolo Simoncelli announced that MotoGP was retiring the No. 58. “This number, from now, belongs to the Simoncelli family,” Ezpeleta said. That last item matters beyond Simoncelli. The 58 joined Kato’s 74 and Tomizawa’s 48 on the sport’s list of retired numbers, alongside honorary retirements for Kevin Schwantz (34) and Loris Capirossi (65). It is a short list, and three of its five numbers belong to riders killed racing. Only the Simoncelli family can reverse the 58’s retirement, and they have not. Simoncelli’s career numbers (14 Grand Prix wins, 31 podiums and one world title, by one count across all classes) are the stat line. The thing people remember is what the sport lost on a Sunday when he was 24 and in the best form of his career. item.title: IndyCar to return to Europe with Barcelona race in 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo IndyCar announced Friday that the IndyCar Series will head to Spain in 2027 for a race at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya – as Motorsport.com previously confirmed . The inaugural IndyCar Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, July 18, 2027. Serving as the centerpiece of Phase Two of the 2027 IndyCar Series schedule, the event will give Barcelona native and five-time champion Alex Palou a home race. The multiyear agreement will be IndyCar’s first race outside North America since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the street circuit of São Paulo, Brazil. It also signals the series' long-awaited return to European soil for the first time since competing at the TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands in 2007. “This is a monumental day for our sport,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “We are pleased to be able to take our ultra-competitive brand of wheel-to-wheel racing to Europe and thrilled that we can showcase IndyCar in Alex Palou’s hometown. We have seen Alex’s remarkable skill and talent for several years and know his fans in Spain have been clamoring to watch him race in person. “We cannot wait to see the NTT IndyCar Series compete at one of the world’s most recognizable motorsports venues set against the backdrop of a very historic and breathtaking international destination like Barcelona.” Palou, 29, won his fifth IndyCar Series championship in 2026. The Chip Ganassi Racing driver became only the second racer in series history to secure four consecutive titles, joining Sebastien Bourdais (2004–07). item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Houston Comets return to the WNBA next season, and they’ve already found a local broadcasting home. On Thursday, the Comets and Tegna announced a multi-year deal that will make it easy for anyone in the Houston market to find games. KTBU Channel 55 and CBS affiliate KHOU 11 (select games) will broadcast Comet games on free TV, while Space City Home Network will simulcast on cable, DirecTV, DirecTV Stream, and Fubo. The network’s direct-to-consumer product, SCHN+, will also stream all games. “Bringing the Comets back to Houston is about reigniting the passion, pride, and energy that have always connected this organization with its fans and community,” said Gretchen Sheirr, President of Business Operations for the Houston Rockets and Comets. “As the WNBA continues to reach new heights, we’re thrilled to partner with TEGNA to make Comets basketball more accessible to fans across the Houston area through free, over-the-air broadcasts on KTBU and additional coverage on KHOU. We’re excited to bring fans closer to the action and deliver outstanding coverage as we begin this exciting new chapter in Comets history.” According to a press release, KHOU will also create exclusive Comets content year-round, providing coverage across its newscasts, 24/7 streaming channel, and digital platforms. “KHOU has covered Houston sports for decades, and the Comets’ homecoming is a story we’ve been waiting to tell,” said David Loving, KHOU’s president and general manager. “As a founding partner, we’re ready to bring Comets action to fans across the region.” The Houston Comets were one of the WNBA’s original eight franchises and won the league’s first four championships. Despite that, the league folded the franchise in 2008 during the height of the Great Recession. This year, the Fertitta family, owners of the NBA’s Houston Rockets, purchased the Connecticut Sun and relocated the team to Houston as the new Houston Comets. Longtime ESPN NBA reporter Kevin Pelton joined the Houston Comets’ front office earlier this year. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...
